title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: open — Examen Cap. IV; immediate vs mediate frame
pass_a_gloss: Caput VI turns to examining Cap. IV. Once more, in the fourth chapter of your book, you spend the entire chapter constituting, polishing, and illustrating the status of the question. We have been held too long in the entryway—starving for the arguments Cap. I had promised we would hear. Still I should stay and talk with you here. You put the question how a personal actual sin can ground everyone's condemnation. A prior distinction is required, and on it the controversy hinges. Take that actual sin as by itself immediately enough to condemn all: then you assume the very point I deny. Take it as enough only through the corruption it bred and spread to all: then I agree.
pass_b_english: CAPUT VI. Examination of Cap. IV. Again in Cap. IV of your treatise you set your hand to constituting, polishing, and illustrating the state of the question; and on that matter you spend the whole of Cap. IV. I am sorry that we are detained so long by you in the vestibule, hungry and eager for your reasons, to the perceiving of which Cap. I of your treatise had invited us. Yet here it becomes me to linger with you a little and converse. It is asked, you say, how that actual sin, which was of a person, suffices for the condemnation of all. But first that point must be presupposed by a distinction: for on it turns the very hinge of this controversy. If you mean that that one actual sin by itself immediately suffices for the condemnation of all men, you presuppose what is in question, and what I deny. But if you mean it suffices for that condemnation by means of the corruption which it produced, propagated into all men, I assent to you.
source_text: CAPUT VI. Examen Cap. IV. Rursus Cap. IV. tui tractatus manum admoves statui quaestionis constituendo, expoliendo, illustrando; inque ea re totum Cap. IV. consumis. Doleo nos tamdiu detineri a te in vestibulo famelicos & appetentes tuarum rationum, ad quas percipiendas nos tui tractatus Cap. primo invitaveras. Hic tamen decet me tecum paulisper commorari, & colloqui. Quaeritur, inquis, quomodo peccatum illud actuale, quod fuit personae, sufficiat ad condemnationem omnium. Atqui prius illud oportet distinctione praesupponendum: in eo enim ipso vertitur cardo hujus controversiae: nam si hoc vis, peccatum illud actuale per se ipsum unum immediate sufficere ad condemnationem omnium hominum, id praesupponis quod versatur in quaestione, quodque ego pernego. Sin vis sufficere ad eam condemnationem mediante corruptione, quam produxit, propagata in omnes homines, tibi assentior.

choices.choice: Vestibule complaint; force immediate vs mediate before answering sufficiency
